description:
Kapfenstein Castle stands on the cone of an extinct volcano about three million years old in the Styrian Vulkanland, near the Slovenian border, and on clear days the view reaches the Koralpe and far into Slovenia, according to the Styrian tourist board. It is first recorded in the 11th century as a defensive castle on the south-eastern edge of Styria.

Since 1918 the castle has belonged to the Winkler-Hermaden family, according to the Styrian tourist board; other sources give 1898 or 1916. According to the Austrian magazine News, the family rebuilt it in the 1940s and turned it into a hotel and restaurant.

Today it is a small family-run castle hotel and restaurant. The family winery, Weingut Winkler-Hermaden, farms vineyards around the castle hill and as far as Klöch, and its wines are served in the castle restaurant, whose kitchen serves Styrian dishes on vine-shaded terraces in good weather and in a knights' hall on cooler days. Breakfast was included on the rate seen, and the season appears to pause in midwinter.
history: Kapfenstein Castle stands on an extinct volcano in the Styrian Vulkanland, near the Slovenian border, and is first recorded in the 11th century as a defensive castle. Since 1918, according to the Styrian tourist board, it has belonged to the Winkler-Hermaden family (other sources give 1898 or 1916), who rebuilt it in the 1940s and turned it into a hotel and restaurant. The family also runs a winery whose vineyards surround the castle hill, and the hotel is run by later generations of the family.

hotel.how_to_stay:
**Getting there:** The castle stands at Kapfenstein 1, on a volcanic hill above the village of Kapfenstein in south-eastern Styria, close to the Slovenian border. Booking lists free private parking with electric charging and accessible parking.

**Rooms & rates:** From approx. €275/night for a 20 m² Standard Double Room with a queen bed, a private bathroom and a flat-screen TV, with buffet breakfast and free cancellation on the rate seen (no payment until shortly before the stay); a 40 m² Standard Suite was around €310. Booking showed the price with taxes and fees included.

**On-site:** A restaurant with terraces and a knights' hall serving Styrian dishes and the family's own wines, and free parking; pets are welcome, with possible fees.

**Good to know:** Rates were seen for one December 2026 night, so check your own dates on Booking. Booking showed no availability for late January, and the castle restaurant lists a season from early March to early December, so the castle appears to close in midwinter. The restaurant opens from Thursday to Sunday, so check the hotel website before you plan dinner.
